### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, touching **8** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`  _(via AUTHORING_RULES (symbol, a top-level const object), runtimeTypes (symbol, a field of const object AUTHORING_RULES))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **215** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **155** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **155**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **100** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **4** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1739f71879f27d10c07fbde77fcf0728ed9abb81` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `8aa6e35abb374d746b019a41f2f1997a7ebced56` — the merge of head `990d41162c5e43bcaaf2df1d4845b916efa851a8` into base `1739f71879f27d10c07fbde77fcf0728ed9abb81`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 8aa6e35abb374d746b019a41f2f1997a7ebced56 && git checkout 8aa6e35abb374d746b019a41f2f1997a7ebced56
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 1739f71879f27d10c07fbde77fcf0728ed9abb81 990d41162c5e43bcaaf2df1d4845b916efa851a8 && git checkout -B drift-repro 1739f71879f27d10c07fbde77fcf0728ed9abb81 && git merge --no-ff 990d41162c5e43bcaaf2df1d4845b916efa851a8

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1739f71879f27d10c07fbde77fcf0728ed9abb81
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 1739f71879f27d10c07fbde77fcf0728ed9abb81` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

No seat comment on the card or the PR was adopted as a number; everything numeric here was re-taken.

① **Right arm, and the premise is real.** On `origin/main`: `packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-plugin.zod.ts` declares `{ type: 'dataset', … allowRuntimeCreate: true, … }`; `TYPE_TO_STACK_KEY` in `packages/lint/src/runtime-gate.ts` reads exactly `flow, object, view, action, page, dashboard, agent, hook, seed, permission, book` (no `dataset`); every `runtimeTypes:` window (`-A3`) in non-test `packages/lint/src/*.ts` naming `dataset` → **0**, ⭐ lit control same grep same corpus naming `'flow'` → **13**. The only file with LIVE `runtimeTypes:` declarations on `origin/main` is `packages/lint/src/authoring-rules.ts` (18 lines); `reference-integrity-suite.ts`, `validate-object-field-refs.ts` and `validate-security-posture.ts` carry the token only in comments — so the PR body's "every declaration sits in `authoring-rules.ts` and `reference-integrity-suite.ts`" is loose on `origin/main` (the suite's per-member declarations arrive WITH this PR), but its conclusion holds. The rules the arm rests on exist and are real, not stubs — read in full and each fired first-hand through the built door (②): `validateDatasetReferences` (`packages/lint/src/validate-dataset-references.ts`, 379 lines; opens `recordsOf(stack.datasets)`, indexes `stack.objects` through `indexObjectGraph`, emits `dataset-include-unknown` / `dataset-field-unknown` / `dataset-field-not-included` / `dataset-filter-field-unknown` at `severity: 'error'`; a member of `REFERENCE_INTEGRITY_RULES`), `validateDatasetMeasureAggregates` (`packages/lint/src/validate-dataset-measure-aggregates.ts`, 245 lines; `recordsOf(stack.datasets)`; emits `measure-aggregate-field-type-refused`; registered in `AUTHORING_RULES` on `origin/main` with `surfaces: CLI_ONLY` and a `surfaceReason` that names the missing `TYPE_TO_STACK_KEY` row as the only thing holding it off the door), and `validateObjectReferences` (`packages/lint/src/validate-object-references.ts`, the `datasets[].object` rung through the `PLATFORM_PROVIDED_OBJECT_NAMES` ladder; `object-reference-unknown` error / `object-reference-unregistered-platform` warning). The host side already carried the collection: `CLOSURE_CONTEXT_KEY_BY_TYPE.dataset = 'datasets'` in `packages/metadata-protocol/src/runtime-authoring-gate.ts` and `listCollection('dataset', 'datasets')` in `protocol.ts`'s per-write gather. Retiring `allowRuntimeCreate` would have thrown away three working rules and a wired host; honouring the declaration (arm A) is the arm the measurement picks.

② **The `seed: 'data'` hazard is discharged by refusal, not by a row.** Off the BUILT `packages/lint/dist/runtime.js` at the head: `stackKeyForType('dataset') = "datasets"`, `runtimeAuthoringRulesFor('dataset') = ["validateDatasetMeasureAggregates", "validateReferenceIntegrity"]`. Production read path, read not asserted: `buildRuntimeWriteSnapshots` lands the written item in `candidate.datasets` (replace-not-erase by name) beside every `CONTEXT_STACK_KEYS` collection; both dataset rules open on `recordsOf(stack.datasets)`; `validateReferenceIntegrity` dispatches per member on `runtimeWriteType`, and exactly `validateObjectReferences` and `validateDatasetReferences` carry `runtimeTypes: ['flow', 'dataset']`. Proof from the mapped collection through the real `runRuntimeAuthoringRules`: a probe with one dangling dimension path and `sum` over a `select` field → `errors=["measure-aggregate-field-type-refused@datasets.probe_ds.measures[0].aggregate", "dataset-field-unknown@datasets.probe_ds.dimensions[0].field"]`; DARK control, same call with `type: 'app'` → `rulesRun=[]`, so a mapping onto nothing is distinguishable from this one. Reverse direction: the host face `evaluateRuntimeAuthoringGate` threads `datasets: mergePendingDeclarations(args.datasets, pending?.datasets)`; `protocol.ts` gathers `datasets` per active write as registry + `sys_metadata` fold (`foldStoredCollection`, both null-org and org scopes) and the batch door accumulates it through `CLOSURE_CONTEXT_KEY_BY_TYPE` — so the snapshot carries `stack.datasets` on every shipped door, and a draft (`state: 'draft'`) is never gated (measured `error=null`). Partial-stack resolution: the crossed rules resolve against `stack.objects` + `stack.datasets` only. Measured on the door: base object absent from the snapshot (`sys_user` removed) with a dangling field → **0 errors** (both dataset rules skip on `graph.has(object)`, and the ladder answers `sys_user` as a known platform name); `sys_no_such_xyz` → advisory only (`object-reference-unregistered-platform`); unprefixed `no_such_object_xyz` → `object-reference-unknown` error; injected `created_at` / `owner_id` as dimensions → clean; dotted path without `include[]` → `dataset-field-not-included`. `objects` alone is narrowed by `narrowObjectsToPackageClosure` when a `packageScope` is present — an unprefixed base object outside the package's declared closure lands on rung ② — which is the #9612 policy every already-gated type carries, not a channel this PR opens.

③ **Blast radius of the new refusal.** (a) Re-taken, not adopted: the corpus was enumerated by path — non-test `defineDataset(` hits under `packages/` and `examples/` are `packages/platform-objects/src/apps/dashboards/system.datasets.ts` (5), `examples/app-showcase/src/ui/datasets/revenue-pulse.dataset.ts` (2) and `chart-gallery.dataset.ts` (2), `examples/app-crm/src/datasets/opportunity.dataset.ts` (1), `examples/app-todo/src/datasets/task.dataset.ts` (1) = **11**; the remaining hits are the definer itself (`packages/spec/src/ui/dataset.zod.ts`) and two hint strings in `validate-widget-bindings.ts` / `validate-chart-bindings.ts`, and `packages/runtime/src/seed-datasets.ts` declares none. All 11 pushed through the real `runRuntimeAuthoringRules` (built lint) AND the real `evaluateRuntimeAuthoringGate` (host face, from source) with their own objects as context (48 platform object defs from `*.object.ts` under `packages/platform-objects/src`, plus showcase 24 / crm 6 / todo 1): **0 errors, 0 advisories, `rulesRun` = 2 on every one, host `accepted` on every one**; `showcase_task_metrics` binds the injected `created_at` and passes. ⭐ Lit control, same harness, same call: the probe above is refused on both faces — `INVALID_METADATA` / `422`, both ids, both name-keyed paths, `rulesRun` 2. Differential: a stored sibling in violation charges nothing to a clean write (0), and the same row as the write IS refused (`dataset-field-unknown@datasets.legacy_ds.dimensions[0].field`). NOT MEASURED: any real tenant's `sys_metadata`-stored datasets, and a booted kernel's registry rather than the object set I assembled from source. (b) Loud and actionable: the receipt is `code: 'INVALID_METADATA'`, `status: 422`, `issues[]` each carrying `rule` / `path` / `where` / `message` / `hint`, plus `rulesRun` (read off the returned error, e.g. `where: dataset "probe_ds" › dimension "stage"`, `hint: Bind the dimension to a field on "crm_opportunity", or to a …`). All six ids the changeset names exist as exported constants: `DATASET_FIELD_UNKNOWN` / `DATASET_FIELD_NOT_INCLUDED` / `DATASET_FILTER_FIELD_UNKNOWN` / `DATASET_INCLUDE_UNKNOWN` in `validate-dataset-references.ts`, `MEASURE_AGGREGATE_FIELD_TYPE_REFUSED` in `validate-dataset-measure-aggregates.ts`, `OBJECT_REFERENCE_UNKNOWN` in `validate-object-references.ts`; the Migration section's clearing steps restate those rules' own `hint` text (the `count` / `count_distinct` sentence is the aggregate rule's hint verbatim in substance) and the example paths match the `datasets.<name>.…` shape the gate emits. Declaration: `.changeset/19143-dataset-runtime-publish-door.md` takes `minor` on both `@objectstack/lint` (published: no `private`, `files: [dist, …]`, exports `.` and `./runtime`) and `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, with no `(narrowing)` arm — the same level and arm the two precedent door-refusal crossings this diff cites landed with (#15254 → `615fac3a0c`, #15495 → `b4b37e599d`, both `minor` on the same two packages). `check-adr-0087-registration --base origin/main` → exit **0** (no declared-breaking changeset); `check-changeset-no-major --base origin/main` → exit **0**; `scripts/pm/check-clause2-carriers.mjs --pair 19272` → exit **0** (claim `Clause-②: yes`, PR body `Clause-②: yes`, `needs:contract-review` in the same state on both carriers). Noted, not acted on: the PR body was edited by a seat after the dev's report (the report says it originally read `no`); it reads `yes` now, which is the state the checks above judged. (c) Nothing crossed fires on a position an author cannot edit: every finding is keyed to `object`, `include[i]`, `dimensions[i].field`, `measures[i].field` / `.aggregate` / `.filter` keys or the dataset `filter` keys; injected system columns resolve rather than refuse; an object the snapshot cannot see is a skip, not a finding; stored siblings cancel. The one refusal whose fix lives outside the dataset document is the package-closure case in ②, whose remedy is a declared dependency — pre-existing policy. Refusal precedence (422 before the ADR-0005 403 for an un-overridable body) is real, both are loud, and the PR changes no ordering. **Real exit codes, private worktree at the head sha**: `pnpm install --offline --frozen-lockfile` → 0; `pnpm --filter '@objectstack/metadata-protocol^...' build` → **0**; `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint test` → **0** (106 files, 3993 tests passed); `pnpm --filter @objectstack/metadata-protocol test` → **0** (181 files passed / 3 skipped, 2590 tests passed / 19 skipped); the changed gate's own files `runtime-authoring-gate.dataset-writes.test.ts` + `protocol.adr0005-org-override-rollback.test.ts` alone → **0** (2 files, 54 tests); `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint --filter @objectstack/metadata-protocol typecheck` → **0** (`tsc --noEmit` clean, `check:test-typecheck: OK`); sweep harness → 0. NOT MEASURED: an ablation (reverting `dataset: 'datasets'` alone and watching `runtime-gate.dataset-writes.test.ts` go red) — I did not run it, so the non-vacuity of the new door controls rests on the refusals I produced through the door rather than on a mutation; repo-wide `pnpm lint`; the 58 derived dispatch-gate families.

Independence — (a) measured first-hand in this act: the three `origin/main` absences with their lit control (object store `215840f435`); the bodies of the three rules and of `buildRuntimeWriteSnapshots` / `runRuntimeAuthoringRules` / `evaluateRuntimeAuthoringGate` / `protocol.ts`'s gather; the wiring readings off the built `dist/runtime.js`; the 11-dataset sweep on both faces with lit, dark, ladder and differential controls; the six rule-id constants; the precedent changesets' levels; every exit code listed in ③. (b) taken from someone else's reading and NOT verified: the PR's repo-wide `pnpm lint` exit 0 and its 58-family dispatch-gates reading; the dev report's statement that the PR body originally carried `Clause-②: no`; the GitHub check-run conclusions (read from the API, not re-run — `Lint & Repo Gates` and `Test Core (5/6)` were still in progress when read); the #7886 38-vs-4 and #7529 3-phantom measurements the docblocks cite.
